the synthesis of the halogen-nitrogen derivatives of indazole, their physico-chemical properties, and their antibacterial effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antibacterial effects of halogen-nitronitrobenzenes, halogen- and hydroxymethylindazoles and their derivatives are not of any importance.
the halogen- and 1-hydroxy-methylindazole derivatives do not exhibit significant antibacterial effects. (orig./MG)
the antibacterial activity of the halogenindazole derivatives is not due to their halogen content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the introduction of a halogen or a nitro group into the indazole molecule does not increase the antibacterial activity.
the 3-halo- and 1-hydroxy- and chloromethyl derivatives 7--23 do not exhibit any antibacterial activity.

the antibacterial properties of the 3-nitroindazoles 1--6, 24--27, 28, 29 and 32--36 and the 3-hydroxymethylinidazoles 8--14, 30 and 31 are not influenced by the introduction of halogen atoms or of a 1-hydroxy-methyl group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a novel and efficient approach for the preparation of halogen-nitrogen indazole derivatives, which are known to have a wide range of biological activities.
the 1,3-dihydroxy-2,3-dihydropyrazine derivatives 24 and 26 are active against gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria.
the 3-chloro derivative 7 is the most potent of these compounds.
